name: hex-to-css-filter-library
description: Library of CSS filters to change the color of an HTML element

paragraphs: A JavaScript library backed by a covering dataset of CSS filters for sRGB: for every one of the 16,777,216 hex colors, the dataset stores a six-function filter chain that — applied to black — renders the target color with a rendered loss under 1%.

Rendered loss is computed from the stored chain itself: black is rendered through invert() sepia() saturate() hue-rotate() brightness() contrast() at floating-point precision, and the absolute per-channel deltas to the target — red, green, blue (0–255) plus hue, saturation, lightness (0–100) — are summed; "under 1%" means that sum is under 1. The metric definition, the statistics, and the dataset schema are documented in docs/dataset.md.
Try it live: the demo page turns any hex color into the stored filter chain in the browser.
features: Search using SPSA by MultiplyByZer0 on Stack Overflow
